# Setup

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(circular)
library(geosphere)

# Set random seed for reproducibility
set.seed(123)
```

# Methods

### Geolocator Error Estimation

```{r geolocator-error-estimation}
# Sample code for geolocator error estimation
# Assuming 'locations' is a dataframe with geolocator data
locations <- data.frame(
  longitude = runif(100, -180, 180),
  latitude = runif(100, -90, 90)
)

# Example calculation of the mean location error
mean_error <- mean(distHaversine(locations[, c('longitude', 'latitude')]))
print(mean_error)
```

### Marine Distance Calculations

```{r marine-distance-calculations}
# Sample code for marine distance calculations
library(geosphere)

# Example points
start_point <- c(-74, 40)
end_point <- c(-73, 41)

# Calculate marine distance
marine_distance <- distHaversine(start_point, end_point)
print(marine_distance)
```

### MC Analysis at Taxa Level

```{r mc-analysis-taxa-level}
# Sample MC analysis code
# Assuming df is the dataframe with taxa data
# df <- data.frame(taxa = c('A', 'B'), connectivity = c(0.1, 0.2))

# Example analysis
mc_analysis <- df %>% group_by(taxa) %>% summarise(mean_connectivity = mean(connectivity))
print(mc_analysis)
```

### Circular Plot Visualization

```{r circular-plot-visualization}
# Sample code for circular plot visualization
# Creating a circular plot of some example data

# Sample data
angles <- circular(runif(100, 0, 2 * pi))

# Plot circular data
plot(angles, main = "Circular Plot Visualization", cex=0.5)
```

# Conclusion

In this analysis, we explored various aspects of migratory connectivity through geolocator analysis, marine distance calculations, and taxa level connectivity analysis, illustrated with circular plots.
